case_data.title: Imaginative Intelligences- Hollywood Edition
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
Imaginative Intelligences was a series of participatory assemblies with creators from across Hollywood's production pipeline: executives, gig workers, creative technologists, and scholars. Over five assemblies in Los Angeles, participants examined a central prompt: "creative purpose at the dawn of AI." 

Depending on the group's makeup, each assembly coalesced around unique themes specific to them. For example, gig workers in session 1 chose pain as their theme, relating to job loss, economic precarity, and what they described as the distinguishing factor between humans and a model. Central to many conversations was the idea of creative purpose: how do creators maintain it as the value and logic behind it increasingly diminishes? Each session generated extensive qualitative material, over 30 hours of recorded conversation, later synthesized into a 35-page report outlining cross-industry pain points and eight design principles to inform more equitable creative-tech development. 

Imaginative Intelligences is a form of collective sense-making: a process that maps where narratives and beliefs around AI land across different sectors of the creative industry.
case_data.headline-findings:
If you have to pay to be in the space that protects your humanity… what the hell's the point?”

1. Creative labor is increasingly precarious and devalued.
Participants repeatedly expressed concern that AI is compounding long-standing
pressures on artists and creatives: invisible labor, derivative training data, and the erosion
of sustainable careers. The emotional tone was often grief, especially among those in film,
music, and media.
One participant described the growing precarity:
“It's become a lot less sustainable for artists to be able to pursue an artistic career if they
do not already come from money. The big fear with AI right now is that this is another way
to devalue the work of artists… because it is “
easy to produce”, because “
all you got to do is
put a bunch of prompts in and generate something out of that””
.
It means that your value as an artist is going to go down, and it means that it's going to be a
lot less sustainable for you to pursue it as a career… Do you know how many gigs I have
right now just to be able to sustain my living right now?... Five… And 20 years ago, I could
have just been able to live off of one of those gigs.”
case_data.inclusion-efforts: We wanted each assembly to have gig workers, creative freelancers, and executives, so we set a limit to however much each group could constitute in our assembly makeup. We tried reaching out to institutional and grassroots players that would have connections to each of these groups for recruitment processes.
case_data.why-is-this-project-important-to-include: This project is uniquely positioned at the intersection of labor and industry: it brought together Hollywood union workers, media executives, and creative technologists in the same participatory process, something no comparable method has done. The eight design principles it produced have already been cited in a California Senate backgrounder, demonstrating real policy impact. Most importantly, the project is preemptive rather than reactive. Where most participatory AI efforts serve as feedback mechanisms on systems already built, Imaginative Intelligences surfaces community-grounded principles before technology is optimized, created, deployed, or regulated, making it a first-mover in shaping more equitable creative-tech development.

Empowerment: Build community power with respect to AI

“So there's this concept of the [Broken Telephone], if I say one thing, I tell to
that person, they tell it to the next person. Eventually after a few cycles, it's going to be a totally different message. But that act of metamorphosis and interpretation of something is the importance of creativity and that aspect of it. So as much as we're focusing on transmission, I think really what we're talking about is also the interpretation of the message and what it means to each act of interpretation from me to you to another person and so on and so on.”
